r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: PASS on the headline asks, FAIL on one contract requirement. Verified by execution: suite 80 passed/26 subtests; --self-test OK; exit band 10-13 provably clear of 1/2/126/127; citable-content, positive-root-proof and three-way discharge all hold. BUT the handoff's 'hash-pin the substitutes so g2 compares against a committed prior declaration' is defeatable: 'orient --substitute <path that does not exist>' writes content_hash='unreadable', is_filler('unreadable') is False, and the record DISCHARGES with exit 0. A pin of the literal string 'unreadable' is not a prior declaration, and a mere typo in a substitute path silently converts a refusal into a satisfied contract. The 'unreadable' sentinel occurs only at scripts/map_orient.py:727 and no test covers it.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: Constraints met. Windows: every write uses encoding='utf-8', newline='\n' (map_orient.py:714, test helpers alike). 3.13+-only API scan CLEAR -- no Path.read_text(newline=), no itertools.batched, no typing.override, no datetime.UTC; the module uses datetime.now(timezone.utc) (3.2+) and open(..., newline='\n'). The sole 'UTC' hit is prose in the receipt-schema docstring. Local 3.14.3 vs CI 3.12 therefore poses no repeat of PR #320's 39 failures. House style honored: module docstring with modes and honest limits, _utf8_stdio(), pure decision layer separated from impure edges, main(argv) + raise SystemExit(main()), --self-test floor. Two-bin rule respected (hash mechanized, declaration content stays prose).

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. Do NOT silently skip this item.

r7-falsifiability.title: CAN THIS CHECK FAIL? (executed mutation)
r7-falsifiability.imperative: Devise a mutation NOT among the shipped three, apply it, run the suite, report red/green with real output. Then attack the harness itself.
r7-falsifiability.finding: ANSWER: YES, THIS CHECK CAN FAIL -- proven by execution, four ways. (1) MY OWN MUTATION M4, not among the shipped three: unmapped_declared 'not any(is_filler)' -> 'not all(is_filler)' (map_orient.py:440). Applied cleanly (count(old) 1->0, count(new) 0->1, source differs). Floor result: exit=0, 42 passed, 0 failed -- MUTANT SURVIVED. Real gap: every filler test in both self_test and PartialFillMatrix uses a SINGLE-element unmapped list, so the per-entry filler rule for multi-entry lists is unpinned; under the mutant, unmapped=['a real thing','n/a'] discharges. (2) The shipped three are GENUINELY EARNED, verified semantically rather than trusting the harness: mutant 3 turns DEGRADED-UNPARSEABLE/exit 10 into RESOLVED/exit 0 on an empty map; mutant 2 turns UNRESOLVABLE-ROOT/exit 11 into DEGRADED-NO-MAP/exit 0 on a bare dir; mutant 1 discharges (exit 0) a record carrying only escalation. Each exhibits wrong BEHAVIOR, not a crash. (3) APPLIED-BEFORE-RED CLAIM CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY and stronger than reported: mutation 2 has TWO subs whose replacement pre-exists (MODE_DEGRADED_NO_MAP 1x, '    return EXIT_OK' 2x), so assertIn(new, mutated) would have passed with nothing substituted; only the count delta proves it landed. Harness refuses a non-matching anchor loudly (HarnessError, 'occurred 0 time(s)', 'This is NOT a killed mutant') and refuses a no-op old==new mutation at STEP 1 with 'HARNESS ERROR ... a red run would be a lie'. (4) HARNESS WEAKNESS FOUND, not blocking: its kill criterion is CLASS-level, not reason-level. Replacing 'proof = probe_root(root)' with a bare raise -- semantically unrelated to any pinned property -- yields exit=1, 22 passed, 25 failed including CitableContent nodes, so all three guards (red, passed>0, node in expect_kills) are satisfied and the harness credits a KILL it did not earn. The mutant produces no verdict at all (exit 1 traceback). Not a BLOCK because the shipped three were verified earned in (2), but the harness cannot self-detect a future collateral kill.
